title: Clearer words, a little character
question: Three layouts on your chosen theme: softer color, clear sans-serif headlines, no approach submenu. Which feels closest?

options.label: The message, up front
options.thesis: A direct introduction with personality carried by color, words and spacing.
options.viewport: Headline and lead side by side, orderly prose beneath, and a clear action before the assessment section.
options.risk: The most editorial option; the two-column opening needs a clear reading order.

options.label: Room to focus
options.thesis: A compact, centered introduction lets the message do the work.
options.viewport: Headline, lead and booking action form one focal point; explanation and a softly tinted assessment section follow.
options.risk: The most familiar structure; distinction comes from precise typography and your voice.

options.label: Work, made clearer
options.thesis: A small diagram connects the everyday problems in the copy to the work of making them easier.
options.viewport: Introduction and three recognizable problems share the opening; a restrained diagram leads into the response and assessment.
options.risk: The diagram earns its space only if it makes the message quicker to understand.
